solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Indian worshipper saving bread for French republican

indicators.note: saving here means keeping something safe inside, so the worshipper holds the bread

parts.note: a Jain is a follower of Jainism, an Indian religion
a cob is a round loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A devout Indian hands over bread to a revolutionary Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescuing, but here it means keeping inside. The Jacobins were the radical club of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobins were a radical political club of the French Revolution, so a member was a republican of that era.

clue.text: All to win, flag best raised

parts.note: a jack is a small flag flown on a ship

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upward, so the word for best is turned around

parts.note: top means best

explanation.surface: Win everything, and run the finest flag up the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the whole prize pool, everything there is to win in a game or lottery.

clue.text: Steroid forming nice torso

indicators.note: forming means making something new, so the letters of nice torso are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drug that builds a lovely body.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortisone is a steroid hormone used medically to reduce inflammation.

clue.text: A hunk climbing in wood

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters go upward, read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick chunk or hunk

explanation.surface: A muscular man scaling a tree in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunk' teases a strapping man; it is just a slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models.

clue.text: Hit yourself

definitions.meaning: slang for oneself, as in looking after you first

explanation.surface: Hit yourself
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is both the top song in the charts and a jocular phrase for one's own self.

clue.text: Performance backfiring after touring Guernsey etc

indicators.note: touring means going round something, so the reversed word travels around the islands
backfiring suggests going backwards, so the word for after is read in reverse

parts.note: after in the sense of later on
Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: A show goes wrong after a tour of the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns the word for after around to give RETAL. Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or spoken performance given to an audience, often by one artist.

clue.text: Hot wingers in rugby?

parts.note: the letters on the wings of the word rugby are its first and last, ..., and that phrase written out in full gives the word

explanation.surface: Rugby's wide men are sexy, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The edges of 'rugby' are R and Y; spell out that phrase in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lustful or sexually aroused, a sense of hot.

clue.text: Indifferent about Michael Caine film — the pits?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for indifferent wraps around the film title

parts.note: cold means unfriendly or indifferent
Alfie is the 1966 film starring Michael Caine

explanation.surface: A lukewarm review of a Michael Caine film calls it the worst.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalfield is an area with coal seams and mines, which are known as pits.

clue.text: Portrait in the end, relative insult

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of Portrait

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: In the end a family member's painting turns out to be an affront.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to provoke with mocking remarks, and a taunt is a jeering insult.

clue.text: Haul fish up with the current

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: to draw is to haul or pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a catch up, going with the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW and EEL together read upwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward means downwind, on the side the wind or current is flowing towards.

clue.text: Pink champagne primarily for the mouth!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of champagne is used

parts.note: oral means relating to or taken by the mouth

explanation.surface: Rosé champagne is meant to be drunk, the clue exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour, named after the sea organism's skeleton.

clue.text: Little blossom in Italy's cut

indicators.note: cut here means inserted, with the short phrase set into the word for blossom

parts.note: to blossom is to develop or mature
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A small flower bloom in Italy has been snipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blossom' looks like a noun, a flower, but it is the verb, to develop. 'cut' tells you to put pieces into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniature is used as an adjective meaning very small, a scaled-down version of something.

clue.text: Greek character not long ago collecting small pieces of paper

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A Greek recently took up gathering scraps of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, and stamps are small pieces of gummed paper.

clue.text: Large wife served with a religious decree

parts.note: large means fat

explanation.surface: A big married woman is handed an edict from the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a ruling on Islamic law issued by a recognised religious authority.

clue.text: Tramp left, getting up, clutching nothing

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so the reversed word grips the zero
getting up means rising, read here as turning the word for left around

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A vagrant departed, rising empty-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT turned around is TROP, which holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: To troop is to walk along heavily or wearily, much as to tramp is.

clue.text: Doctor in a pretty kind of suit

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of in a pretty are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor looking smart in a nice suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is a verb meaning to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A paternity suit is a lawsuit to establish who fathered a child, not clothing.

clue.text: Driving book

definitions.meaning: out travelling by car, a phrase for being on a journey
Jack Kerouac's novel of the Beat Generation

explanation.surface: Driving book
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the road means travelling, and it is also the title of Kerouac's 1957 novel.

clue.text: Those shelled, when bombed resist too

indicators.note: bombed suggests blown apart, so the letters of resist too are scattered

explanation.surface: Troops under shellfire also hold out when bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' suggests artillery; it means having shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoises are reptiles that carry a hard shell on their backs.

clue.text: Sick of Man United say, old menace

parts.note: Manchester United is a football club, FC
to lour is to look threatening or menacing

explanation.surface: A football fan feels ill at an ageing threat to Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Off colour is a British idiom for slightly unwell, looking a bit poorly.

clue.text: Ashes evidently lost, did you say, for group of stars?

indicators.note: asking what was said signals that the sound of the phrase gives the answer

parts.note: a grate bare of ashes, i.e. an empty fireplace grate, spoken as two words

explanation.surface: A cricket fan asks about losing the Ashes, then about constellations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England–Australia cricket series, but here ashes are what sits in a fire grate; with them gone the grate is bare.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation, a named pattern of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Weak — becoming wk?

definitions.meaning: the word week with its middle, its gut, taken out leaves wk

explanation.surface: Weak, or is it shortened to wk?
explanation.definitionFit: Gutless means cowardly and weak, and literally names a word with its insides removed.

clue.text: Novelist, certainly English

parts.note: defo is British slang for definitely

explanation.surface: A writer is definitely an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, one of the earliest English novels.

clue.text: Heading for execution, relative hiding in tree — that's hairy!

indicators.note: a heading is the start, so only the first letter of execution is taken
hiding in means concealed inside, so the relative goes within the tree

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
bro is short for brother, a relative

explanation.surface: Bound for the gallows, a family member hides up a tree: a hairy moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy' looks like slang for frightening; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is the strip of hair above the eye, so it is a hairy feature.

clue.text: Weapon trademarked, and stunning errant rogues, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A branded stun weapon is used on wayward villains.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun firing electrified darts, a weapon to incapacitate people.

clue.text: Fight delicious? O my!

indicators.note: O is nothing, so the word my is reduced to zero and dropped

parts.note: scrummy is British slang for delicious
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a tasty treat, then asks if it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly struggle or scramble, as well as the rugby formation.

clue.text: Free service's ending, pay ladies and gentlemen to go ahead

indicators.note: going ahead means being placed in front, so these pieces come before the final letter

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
the ladies and the gents are toilets, loos in British slang

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word service

explanation.surface: Free service at the end, but you must pay to use the public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes only the final letter of 'service's', E; 'to go ahead' puts the other pieces in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means unattached, at liberty to go anywhere and do anything.

clue.text: Up-ended drink dealt with

indicators.note: up-ended means turned on its head, so in a down clue the drink is read upwards

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: A drink tipped over and handled.
explanation.definitionFit: To have faced a problem is to have confronted it and dealt with it.

clue.text: Far Eastern city in Nepal has appeared

indicators.note: in signals that the city's letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An Asian city has turned up in Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, a city in the Himalayas of Asia.

clue.text: Parts attached to side of head, each terribly precise

definitions.text: Parts attached to side of head

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of precise are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Every part fixed beside the head is awfully exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Earpieces are the arms of glasses or parts of headphones that sit at the ears.

clue.text: Fury has no limits after a second affair

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word behind the first pieces

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: with its limits gone the word Fury loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rage boils over briefly in a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, especially a secret one, from the French for love.

clue.text: Kind of dog, someday barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of someday go wild

explanation.surface: A dog breed that some day will be barking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian breed of dog bred for herding and sledging.

clue.text: Fish caught by female bird

indicators.note: caught by means held within, so the female animal surrounds the fish

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A fish is snapped up by a hen bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, common in towns and gardens.
